med_ex
v0.1.0

    Host integration

    Copy Markdown View Source

    This guide covers everything a Phoenix or Elixir host needs to capture indexed mono PCM16LE audio with MedEx.Capture, stream an independent live Opus preview over MedEx.Preview, and serve MedEx's packaged browser helpers.

    Prerequisites

    • Elixir ~> 1.20 (tested on Elixir 1.20.5 / OTP 29.1.2).
    • Ubuntu 26.04 native build packages for WebRTC (ex_dtls, ex_libsrtp): build-essential, pkg-config, and libssl-dev.
    • Live Opus encoding uses membrane_opus_plugin, which uses precompiled libopus binaries on supported Linux/macOS targets (install libopus-dev if compiling libopus from source).
    • Browser microphone capture (getUserMedia + AudioWorklet) requires a secure context (https://, or http://localhost / http://127.0.0.1 for local dev).

    1. Serve the packaged browser assets

    MedEx.Web.asset_path/1 resolves the three JavaScript files shipped inside :med_ex:

    • "session_hook.js" — LiveView hook helper (createMedExHook/1) for the clinician's receive-only WebRTC preview.
    • "pcm_capture.js" — patient-browser capture helper (startPCM/4).
    • "pcm_worklet.js" — AudioWorkletProcessor ("med-ex-indexed-pcm") loaded by startPCM/4.

    Serve all three as application/javascript from your endpoint:

    defp serve_med_ex_assets(%Plug.Conn{path_info: ["med_ex", name]} = conn, _opts)
     when name in ~w(session_hook.js pcm_capture.js pcm_worklet.js) do
  conn
  |> Plug.Conn.put_resp_content_type("application/javascript")
  |> Plug.Conn.send_file(200, MedEx.Web.asset_path(name))
  |> Plug.Conn.halt()
end

defp serve_med_ex_assets(conn, _opts), do: conn

    2. Supervise live capture in your host

    Start a host-owned DynamicSupervisor (and optionally a Registry if preview channels need to look up active captures by encounter). MedEx starts no global capture processes.

    # In your application supervision tree:
children = [
  {Registry, keys: :unique, name: MyApp.ActiveCapture},
  {DynamicSupervisor, strategy: :one_for_one, name: MyApp.Captures}
]

    For the preview example below, start {Phoenix.PubSub, name: MyApp.PubSub} in the host supervisor as well. Register the encounter in MyApp.ActiveCapture from the producer process and broadcast after the capture starts.

    Each capture process takes :owner, :acquisition_id, and :artifact_dir:

    {:ok, _} = Registry.register(MyApp.ActiveCapture, encounter_id, nil)

{:ok, capture} =
  DynamicSupervisor.start_child(
    MyApp.Captures,
    {MedEx.Capture,
     owner: self(),
     acquisition_id: acquisition_id,
     artifact_dir: artifact_dir}
  )

Registry.update_value(MyApp.ActiveCapture, encounter_id, fn _ -> capture end)
Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(MyApp.PubSub, "preview:" <> encounter_id, {:capture_started, capture})

    MedEx.Capture monitors :owner and aborts (deleting its temporary .part file) if :owner exits before finish/1.

    Handling binary PCM WebSocket frames

    In your authenticated WebSocket handler (e.g. a WebSock module), decode each binary frame as an 8-byte unsigned big-endian starting sample index followed by PCM16LE bytes, push to MedEx.Capture.push/3, and reply with text "ack":

    def handle_in({<<index::unsigned-big-64, pcm::binary>>, [opcode: :binary]}, state) do
  case MedEx.Capture.push(state.capture, index, pcm) do
    :ok -> {:push, {:text, "ack"}, state}
    {:error, _reason} -> {:stop, :normal, 1008, {:text, "invalid_capture"}, state}
  end
end

def handle_in({"finish", [opcode: :text]}, state) do
  case MedEx.Capture.finish(state.capture) do
    {:ok, %MedEx.Evidence{} = evidence} ->
      # Persist finalized evidence before closing the socket.
      :ok = MyApp.ClinicalStore.record_ready(state.encounter_id, evidence)
      {:stop, :normal, 1000, {:text, "ready"}, state}

    {:error, _reason} ->
      {:stop, :normal, 1011, {:text, "capture_failed"}, state}
  end
end

    Capture rules and error returns

    Rule / OperationBehavior
    Sample formatMono 48 kHz signed 16-bit little-endian PCM (PCM16LE).
    Frame sizeEven byte count in 2..1920 (up to 960 samples / 20 ms). Only one short tail frame (< 1920 bytes) is allowed, immediately before finish/1.
    Contiguity & limitfirst_sample must start at 0 and advance contiguously without gaps, up to 30 minutes (86_400_000 samples). Violations return {:error, :invalid_frame} and stop the capture.
    finish/1Returns {:ok, %MedEx.Evidence{}}, {:error, :empty_capture} (0 samples pushed), {:error, :artifact_conflict} (existing file digest mismatch), or {:error, posix}.
    Preview fan-outOnly full 1,920-byte frames are offered to the preview encoder. Preview lag, drop, or encoder exit never blocks or aborts WAV capture.

    MedEx.Evidence fields

    MedEx.Capture.finish/1 returns %MedEx.Evidence{}:

    FieldValue
    :acquisition_idHost-provided acquisition ID string
    :artifact_keyContent-addressed filename ("<file_sha256>.wav")
    :file_sha256Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the complete WAV file
    :pcm_sha256Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw PCM16LE bytes
    :kind:audio_pcm16_wav
    :sample_rate_hz48_000
    :first_sample0 (inclusive)
    :end_sampleExclusive ending sample index
    :sample_countTotal captured mono samples
    :continuity:observed_continuous

    3. Wire the preview signaling channel

    The clinician's Phoenix Channel owns one replaceable MedEx.Preview peer. MedEx.Preview.answer/2 sends {:ex_webrtc, peer.pid, {:connection_state_change, state}} messages to the channel process. Once :connected, subscribe the channel to the active MedEx.Capture (only one subscriber is active at a time; a newer subscriber replaces the previous one).

    defmodule MyAppWeb.PreviewChannel do
  use Phoenix.Channel

  alias MedEx.{Capture, Preview}

  @impl true
  def join("signaling:" <> encounter_id, %{"connection_id" => id}, socket)
      when is_binary(id) do
    # Authorize socket.assigns here before allowing join.
    {:ok, %{session_id: encounter_id},
     assign(socket,
       encounter_id: encounter_id,
       peer: nil,
       capture: nil,
       sequence: 0,
       clock: nil,
       connected: false
     )}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_in("offer", %{"sdp" => sdp}, %{assigns: %{peer: nil}} = socket) do
    opts = [ice_servers: Application.get_env(:my_app, :ice_servers, [])]

    case Preview.answer(sdp, opts) do
      {:ok, peer, answer_sdp} ->
        {:reply, {:ok, %{sdp: answer_sdp}}, assign(socket, :peer, peer)}

      {:error, _reason} ->
        {:reply, {:error, %{reason: "negotiation_failed"}}, socket}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info(
        {:ex_webrtc, pid, {:connection_state_change, :connected}},
        %{assigns: %{peer: %{pid: pid}, connected: false}} = socket
      ) do
    encounter_id = socket.assigns.encounter_id
    :ok = Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(MyApp.PubSub, "preview:" <> encounter_id)

    case Registry.lookup(MyApp.ActiveCapture, encounter_id) do
      [{_producer, capture}] when is_pid(capture) -> send(self(), {:capture_started, capture})
      _ -> :ok
    end
    {:noreply, assign(socket, :connected, true)}
  end

  def handle_info({:capture_started, capture}, %{assigns: %{connected: true}} = socket) do
    case Capture.subscribe(capture) do
      :ok ->
        {:noreply, assign(socket, :capture, capture)}

      {:error, :preview_unavailable} ->
        push(socket, "preview_failed", %{})
        {:noreply, socket}
    end
  catch
    :exit, _ -> {:noreply, socket}
  end

  def handle_info(
        {:med_ex_preview, capture, sample_index, packet},
        %{assigns: %{capture: capture, peer: peer, sequence: seq, clock: clock}} = socket
      ) do
    tick = next_tick(clock, capture, sample_index)
    :ok = Preview.send_opus(peer, packet, seq, tick)
    :ok = Capture.demand(capture)
    {:noreply, assign(socket, sequence: seq + 1, clock: {capture, sample_index, tick})}
  end

  def handle_info({:med_ex_preview_failed, capture, _reason}, %{assigns: %{capture: capture}} = socket) do
    push(socket, "preview_failed", %{})
    {:noreply, assign(socket, :capture, nil)}
  end

  def handle_info(
        {:ex_webrtc, pid, {:connection_state_change, state}},
        %{assigns: %{peer: %{pid: pid}}} = socket
      )
      when state in [:failed, :closed],
      do: {:stop, :normal, socket}

  def handle_info(_msg, socket), do: {:noreply, socket}

  @impl true
  def terminate(_reason, socket) do
    if peer = socket.assigns[:peer], do: Preview.close(peer)
    :ok
  end

  # Keep RTP media timestamps monotonic if a new capture starts on the same peer.
  defp next_tick(nil, _capture, index), do: index
  defp next_tick({capture, last, tick}, capture, index), do: tick + index - last
  defp next_tick({_prev, _last, tick}, _capture, _index), do: tick + 960
end

    Pass :ice_servers to MedEx.Preview.answer/2 and iceServers to createMedExHook/1 for host-managed STUN/TURN configuration. The default [] uses direct local candidates.

    4. Browser preview hook (session_hook.js)

    Wrap the clinician preview controls in a LiveView container with phx-update="ignore" (required so LiveView DOM diffs do not tear down the active <audio> stream), data-token (sent in Phoenix Socket params), an <audio> element, and an optional [role="status"] element:

    <section
  id="diagnostic-preview"
  phx-hook="MedExSessionHook"
  phx-update="ignore"
  data-token={@socket_token}
  data-encounter-id={@encounter_id}
>
  <button id="preview-play" type="button">Play preview</button>
  <button id="preview-disconnect" type="button">Disconnect</button>
  <button id="preview-reconnect" type="button">Reconnect</button>
  <audio autoplay playsinline></audio>
  <p role="status">idle</p>
</section>

    Register the hook on your LiveSocket:

    import { Socket } from "/assets/phoenix.mjs";
import { LiveSocket } from "/assets/phoenix_live_view.esm.js";
import { createMedExHook } from "/med_ex/session_hook.js";

const csrfToken = document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]').content;
const liveSocket = new LiveSocket("/live", Socket, {
  params: { _csrf_token: csrfToken },
  hooks: {
    MedExSessionHook: createMedExHook({
      Socket,
      socketPath: "/socket",
      topic: el => "signaling:" + el.dataset.encounterId,
      play: "#preview-play",
      disconnect: "#preview-disconnect",
      reconnect: "#preview-reconnect",
      iceServers: []
    })
  }
});
liveSocket.connect();

    Channel protocol expected by createMedExHook:

    1. Joins topic(el) with { connection_id: crypto.randomUUID() }, expecting { session_id }.
    2. Gathers browser ICE candidates and pushes "offer" with { sdp }, expecting { sdp } answer.
    3. Handles server-pushed "preview_failed" by closing the peer cleanly and displaying a retry status without affecting capture.

    5. Browser live PCM capture (pcm_capture.js & pcm_worklet.js)

    Call startPCM from a user gesture, such as clicking Start. Provide separate buttons with IDs finish-capture and abort-capture. Enable Finish from the recording callback once the server acknowledges the first frame.

    import { startPCM } from "/med_ex/pcm_capture.js";

const socket = new WebSocket("wss://example.test/pcm");
await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  socket.onopen = resolve;
  socket.onerror = reject;
  socket.onclose = reject;
});

const handle = await startPCM(
  socket,
  "/med_ex/pcm_worklet.js",
  outcome => console.log("Capture ended:", outcome),
  () => console.log("Recording active (first frame acknowledged)")
);

// Use separate buttons for the two terminal actions.
document.querySelector("#finish-capture").onclick = () => handle.finish();
document.querySelector("#abort-capture").onclick = () => handle.abort();

    Live PCM wire protocol and outcome codes

    • Audio constraints: AudioContext({ sampleRate: 48000 }) (fails with "setup_failed" if the browser context cannot run at 48 kHz) and getUserMedia with channelCount: { exact: 1 } and echoCancellation, noiseSuppression, and autoGainControl set to { exact: false }.
    • Binary frames: 8-byte unsigned big-endian first_sample index followed by up to 960 mono PCM16LE samples (1,920 bytes).
    • Flow control: The worklet starts with 8 in-flight frame credits. The host must reply with text "ack" after accepting each frame. After the first "ack", startPCM/4 invokes onRecording().
    • Normal finish: handle.finish() drains any final partial frame, sends text "finish", and waits for the host's terminal text frame (for example "ready" or "capture_failed").
    • Startup & gap rules: Allow up to 1 second for continuous microphone startup ("capture_source_timeout" if no samples arrive). Any source gap after the first frame ends capture with "capture_gap".

    Terminal strings delivered to onOutcome(outcome):

    OutcomeMeaning
    Host text frame (e.g. "ready", "capture_failed", "invalid_capture")Any non-"ack" text message sent by the host closes capture with that string.
    "setup_failed"Microphone permission/constraints, 48 kHz context, worklet load, or socket pre-check failed (startPCM/4 also rejects).
    "capture_source_timeout"No audio samples arrived within 1 second of start or during an empty-input stall.
    "capture_gap"AudioWorklet detected a discontinuity in currentFrame after capture became active.
    "capture_overflow"All 8 in-flight frame credits were exhausted without host "ack" replies.
    "source_ended"Browser media track ended unexpectedly.
    "disconnected"WebSocket closed or errored before a terminal host outcome arrived.
    "aborted"Host browser code called handle.abort().
